prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1076; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and a neck strain. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been asked to provide any medical records directly.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the accident happened, and scene photos are consistent with it.

Entry 3: The neck strain is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. Initial treatment was conservative, consistent with the reported symptoms.

Entry 4: Claimant's medical history shows a small strain in the same area years ago, which healed fully with no ongoing complaints at the time. Records from that episode are being requested for comparison.

Entry 5: Treatment has grown to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits. New body areas were added to the claim several weeks after the crash, and it is not yet clear whether all of the reported damage came from this impact.

Entry 6: Claimant has since added small details to the account, but the core description of the collision has stayed the same across each statement. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests damage predates the policy start date.

Entry 7: The driver is named on the policy. Pending receipt of the requested medical records and an independent medical review, the file will remain open for evaluation of the treatment scope and its relationship to the collision.
